intro: A Nashville fiddle duo of adventurous acoustic interplay.
story: 10 String Symphony is a Nashville duo of two fiddlers, Rachel Baiman, a former Illinois state fiddle champion, and Christian Sedelmyer, a classically trained violinist who tours with the Jerry Douglas Band; the name comes from their two five-string fiddles. Baiman has said the band has no rules about what it can sound like, and they want a full sound, the idea of a symphony. Their debut, Weight of the World, came out in 2015, drew attention from NPR's All Songs Considered and reached number 3 on the Billboard Bluegrass chart. They played Pickathon in 2016. Their third album, Generation Frustration, produced by Kris Drever, came out in July 2018, and NPR's World Cafe Nashville featured them that September.
artist_reel_line: Their third album, Generation Frustration, came out in July 2018.

intro: A Portland neo-soul vocalist.
story: Blossom is Keisha Chiddick, a Portland R&B singer who opened the Mt. Hood Stage on the Friday of Pickathon 2016. Willamette Week named her its Best of Portland at the festival, and Vortex heard severely chilled-out R&B. The Portland Mercury's 2018 list of local bands to hear named her, praising her live show and the song "Superwoman." She went on to release local favorites such as Maybe and sang in the city's Mercury Music Series in 2021.

intro: A country duo from the Pickathon family.
story: Caleb Klauder was raised on Orcas Island and was a founding member of Foghorn Stringband; Reeb Willms joined him in Portland, and the two lead a Portland country scene together. Innocent Road, on West Sound in September 2016, was Klauder's first country record in six years, and NPR Music's Songs We Love picked "There Goes My Love," calling them two of the finest traditional musicians in America. They played Pickathon in 2016, after Klauder's visits in 2001, 2007 and 2013, and again in 2018. Gold in Your Pocket came out on Free Dirt on November 15, 2024.
artist_reel_line: Innocent Road came out in September 2016, and NPR picked a song.

intro: A Portland queer retro-futurist R&B singer.
story: Chanti Darling is Chanticleer Tru, who formed the retro-futurist R&B project in 2015 after his band Magic Mouth ended; two dancers perform at every show. In March 2016 it won Willamette Week's Best New Band poll, and the premise, Tru says, was telling indie guys who call themselves R&B to step aside. They played Pickathon that summer. RNB Vol. 1, with production help from Damon Boucher, came out on Tender Loving Empire in August 2018.

intro: An Athens, Georgia band of harmonized cosmic country.
story: Futurebirds formed in Athens, Georgia, in 2008, among University of Georgia students, and put out Hampton's Lullaby on Autumn Tone on July 27, 2010. Baba Yaga followed in 2013 on Fat Possum and Hotel Parties in 2015 on Easy Sound; Stereogum called it a meditation on life on the road. They played Pickathon in 2016. Teamwork came out in 2020 on VL4L Records and the live album Thanks Ya'll in 2023. Ten years after the farm, they are on the road through the South behind the double album Far Out Country, from June 2026.

intro: A Dublin band of Irish storytelling and string-band drive.
story: I Draw Slow came back to Pickathon in 2016, three years after their first visit. The Dublin five-piece is built around the siblings Dave and Louise Holden, and blends Irish folk with American bluegrass and old-time. Turn Your Face to the Sun came out on Compass Records in 2017, and a self-titled album followed after the pandemic. They still tour internationally on the folk and Celtic circuit.

intro: A North Carolina trio of Southern-rooted indie rock.
story: Mount Moriah are from Durham, North Carolina, a band of Heather McEntire, formerly of Bellafea, and Jenks Miller of Horseback. The self-titled debut came out in 2011, and Miracle Temple, their second album and first for Merge, on February 26, 2013; Paste named them one of its Best of What's Next on the strength of it. They came to Pickathon in 2016 behind How to Dance. H.C. McEntire has since turned to solo records and conservation writing.

intro: An Icelandic-Swedish duo of whispered harmonies.
story: My Bubba began when Bubba Tomasdottir answered an ad to share My Larsdotter's Copenhagen apartment and the two started singing together that day. How It's Done in Italy came out in 2010 and Goes Abroader, produced by Noah Georgeson, in 2014. Big Bad Good followed on April 15, 2016, the year of their Pickathon set. A single on Third Man Records came in 2017, and they played WOMADelaide in Australia in 2018.

intro: A Portland rapper of conversational rhymes.
story: Myke Bogan is a Portland rapper whose laid-back, conversational rhymes made him a hometown favorite at Pickathon in 2016, where KEXP said he kicked off the weekend's action. He still releases music from the Northwest, and in September 2025 he put out the EP Text me when he leaves.

intro: A Montreal songwriter of cinematic chamber-pop.
story: Patrick Watson was born in Lancaster, California, and raised in Hudson, Quebec, and the Montreal band he leads once lived in an abandoned church. Close to Paradise won the 2007 Polaris Music Prize, beating Arcade Fire's Neon Bible, and Wooden Arms was shortlisted in 2009. Love Songs for Robots came out on Domino in May 2015, was longlisted for the Polaris and reached number three in Canada. They played Pickathon in 2016. Wave followed in October 2019, Uh Oh in 2025, and in November 2026 he toured Australia.

intro: A Nashville country-rock quartet.
story: Promised Land Sound formed in Nashville around 2012 from the circles of PUJOL, JEFF the Brotherhood and Those Darlins, and Rolling Stone profiled them as Nashville's garage-psych heroes. Jack White's Third Man Records released a live 7-inch in 2013, the year of their self-titled debut on Paradise of Bachelors. For Use and Delight followed on October 2, 2015, and they came to Pickathon the next summer.

intro: A California country duo.
story: The Easy Leaves, Kevin Carducci and Sage Fifield of Santa Rosa, California, played Pickathon for a second summer in a row in 2016. They formed in 2008 with harmonies in the tradition of the Louvin and Everly brothers, and American Times, from 2012, had a video that reached CMT. Their public performances taper off around 2020.

intro: A Texas sibling duo of stomp-and-holler folk-rock.
story: Tyler and Maggie Heath formed the Oh Hellos in 2011 in San Marcos, Texas, after writing a song for their mother's birthday, and they stay independent. Through the Deep, Dark Valley, from 2012, was self-produced, and Dear Wormwood, from 2015, is a concept album built on The Screwtape Letters that they called C.S. Lewis fanfiction. They played Pickathon in 2016. Tyler told NPR in 2017 that "Torches" is about violent nationalism and tribalism. After a long break they came back in fall 2025 with a farewell-for-now tour called Yours Truly.

intro: A Los Angeles trio of three-part harmonies.
story: The Wild Reeds formed in Los Angeles in 2010 around Sharon Silva, Kinsey Lee and Mackenzie Howe. Blind and Brave came out in 2014 and the Best Wishes EP in May 2016, and they said they had been trying to play Pickathon for years. Saving Country Music named them the band to watch coming out of the festival. The World We Built, their major-label debut, came on Dualtone in 2017, and a third LP, Cheers, in 2019. In October 2025 Silva released her debut solo album, Underachiever.

intro: A Portland post-punk trio.
story: The Woolen Men are Lawton Browning, Raf Spielman and Alex Geddes of Portland, who signed to Woodsist in 2012 after a string of cassettes and singles. A self-titled debut came in early 2013, and Temporary Monument, on Woodsist on September 4, 2015, took on gentrification in Portland; the Portland Mercury said the common enemy of a squirming local scene is New Portland. They played Pickathon in 2016. Post followed in 2018, a less angry record, and they told Bandcamp Daily they did not want to make Temporary Monument 2.
artist_reel_line: Post, in 2018, was a less angry record, and no sequel to Temporary Monument.

intro: An Asheville bluegrass band, back for a third visit.
story: Town Mountain is an Asheville, North Carolina, bluegrass and honky-tonk string band, with a debut, Original Bluegrass and Roots, in 2007. They won an IBMA Momentum Award in 2013, and played Pickathon in 2009, 2010 and 2016. Southern Crescent came out in 2016, and New Freedom Blues, their sixth album, on October 26, 2018, produced by Caleb Klauder at Echo Mountain Studios; Bluegrass Today called it another high point in their trajectory. They came back to the farm in 2019, and Lines in the Levee followed on New West on October 7, 2022.

intro: A London guitar-pop duo of Velvet Underground melodies.
story: Ultimate Painting is the London duo of Jack Cooper of Mazes and James Hoare of Veronica Falls, formed in 2014 after their bands toured together. Green Lanes came a year before Dusk, their third album, which came out on Trouble in Mind in 2016, the year of their Pickathon set. In February 2018 Cooper announced the band was over and that the Bella Union album Up! would not be released, blaming an irreconcilable breakdown with Hoare.

intro: A metal supergroup of the Bay Area and Northwest.
story: VHÖL brings together Mike Scheidt of YOB, John Cobbett of Ludicra, Aesop Dekker of Agalloch and Sigrid Sheie of Hammers of Misfortune. Deeper Than Sky, from 2015 on Profound Lore, was behind them when Pickathon's talent buyer booked them in 2016, despite the band being only intermittently active. The Portland Mercury called their set the festival's first metal performance, with teens moshing up front and returning the next day. Scheidt's YOB made its own Pickathon debut in 2019, which the Mercury tied back to Vhol.

intro: A honky-tonk supergroup of three-part harmonies.
story: Western Centuries is a Seattle-based roots band of Cahalen Morrison, Ethan Lawton and Jim Miller, a founding member of Donna the Buffalo, all three writing and singing, a band without a leader. Weight of the World came out in 2016, with pedal steel from Rusty Blake, and Green Man Review called it country and western made the way it should be. They played Pickathon that year. Call the Captain, their third album, came out on Free Dirt Records on April 3, 2020.

intro: Ravid Kahalani's Yemenite funk and jazz ensemble.
story: Ravid Kahalani, an Israeli singer born in 1978 to a Yemenite family, founded Yemen Blues in 2010 with the bassist Omer Avital, after five years singing with Idan Raichel's project. Yemen Blues came out in 2011 and Insaniya in 2015; DownBeat reviewed Insaniya in December 2016, the year they played Pickathon. Only Love Remains followed on Kartel Music Group, and they were in studio at WNYC Soundcheck on September 16, 2024. They still tour internationally, with club dates in Berlin and New York in fall 2026.
